name: Citizenship by Marriage (Stateless Spouse Only)

requirements.blocker_text: Article 8 states marriage to an Uzbek citizen does NOT itself change either spouse's citizenship. The only marriage-linked reduction found: a STATELESS person married to an Uzbek citizen may apply for citizenship after 3 years' continuous residence (Article 19, second section), versus the standard 5-year residency track that applies to everyone else, married or not.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 3 years' continuous residence as a stateless spouse of a citizen, then apply.

sources.title: ecoi.net -- hosted text of the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan 'On Citizenship,' Article 8 (marriage does not change citizenship) and Article 19 (stateless-spouse 3-year reduced residency)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uzbekistan). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2-hosted-primary-text limitation as uz_citizenship_by_descent.json; this dataset's validator requires tier-1 sourcing to publish a hard requirement, so this stays draft pending a direct lex.uz citation. UNUSUAL FINDING, WORTH FLAGGING AGAINST THE DOMINANT PATTERN IN THIS DATASET: Uzbekistan's law confers NO citizenship benefit at all to an ordinary FOREIGN-NATIONAL spouse (of either gender) married to an Uzbek citizen -- Article 8 explicitly rules this out. The only marriage-adjacent reduction in the law applies exclusively to a STATELESS spouse (3 years vs. the standard 5), which is not really a 'marriage privilege' for foreign nationals generally so much as a narrow statelessness-mitigation clause that happens to require marriage to a citizen as its trigger. This is a genuinely different shape from every other country's marriage-citizenship route built in this dataset (all of which give SOME reduction, however asymmetric, to at least one gender of ordinary foreign national spouse) -- Uzbekistan gives NONE. Filed under 'settled' rather than omitted entirely because the stateless-spouse mechanism is real, sourced, and marriage-triggered, not because it functions like the marriage routes built for other countries. dual_citizenship_allowed set false given the naturalization law's general renunciation requirement (see uz_citizenship_naturalisation.json), which a stateless applicant trivially satisfies by definition (no other citizenship to renounce).
